mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-86.3 to -81.1). This momentum reflects a gradual, self-reinforcing resumption of shopping and leisure trips as households adapt to eased restrictions, and the trend will continue upward over the next four weeks absent a new shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -86.3 to -81.1 over three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days, breaking the three-week monotonic improvement pattern.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility jumped sharply from -62.1 to -51.3 between t-2w and t-1w, a discrete 10.8-point gain exceeding typical weekly noise. Such a jump signals a formal policy easing (e.g. permitted outdoor movement) that, once crossed, also unlocks retail visits within 1-2 weeks as the same relaxation applies to shops.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -62.1 to -51.3 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks following a PARKS jump greater than 8 points, or RETAIL_REC mean next 28 days is below last 28 days mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES have both improved together over the last three weeks (TRANSIT -79.4 to -75.1; WORKPLACES -69.6 to -65.3). Their joint recovery indicates commuting-linked trip chaining, where workers combine commute trips with retail stops, so simultaneous improvement in both series amplifies RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improved every week over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no greater than would be predicted by TRANSIT or WORKPLACES alone, indicating no synergistic interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL time has steadily declined from 28.1 to 24.7 over the snapshot, indicating households are spending less time at home as spring weather and loosened confinement rules take hold. In a reopening regime, this declining home-dwelling trend frees time for retail and recreation trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 28.1 to 24.7 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise even as RESIDENTIAL continues its decline, or RESIDENTIAL reverses upward while RETAIL_REC still rises, breaking the inverse coupling.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility recovered sharply in the most recent week, rising from -45.6 to -39.9 to -39.0, well ahead of RETAIL_REC's recovery pace. As a leading indicator of general willingness to leave home for non-essential errands, this faster grocery recovery should pull RETAIL_REC higher within one week as consumers extend the same outings to retail stops.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved by 6.6 points between t-2w and t-1w while RETAIL_REC improved by only 2.9 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the week immediately following a GROCERY_PHARM improvement exceeding the prior RETAIL_REC weekly gain.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility improvement has slowed its pace (0.9 points t-3w to t-2w, 2.7 points t-2w to t-1w, 0.7 points t-1w to t-0w), suggesting the initial reopening phase for workplaces is plateauing. If WORKPLACES weekly change falls below 1 point for two consecutive weeks, this signals policy-driven saturation that will likewise cap RETAIL_REC growth over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly change falls below 1 point for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES weekly gains were 0.9, 2.7, 0.7 points across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to grow at its prior pace or accelerates despite WORKPLACES weekly gains staying below 1 point for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility is recovering much faster than RESIDENTIAL is declining (PARKS up 15.8 points vs RESIDENTIAL down only 3.4 points over the snapshot). This divergence suggests outdoor leisure is substituting for in-home time disproportionately, and when combined with continued RESIDENTIAL decline, the interaction amplifies retail recovery as people combine park visits with nearby shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly gain exceeds 3x the RESIDENTIAL weekly decline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose 15.8 points while RESIDENTIAL fell only 3.4 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth is not larger than predicted by PARKS or RESIDENTIAL individually, indicating no amplifying interaction between the two series.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-May seasonal warming in Lombardy typically increases outdoor and shopping activity independent of policy; PARKS mobility already shows strong week-on-week gains consistent with this seasonal pull, which should translate into a short-term bump in RETAIL_REC within one week as warmer weather draws people out.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved every week of the snapshot, reaching -51.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the week immediately following continued PARKS improvement, suggesting seasonal effects are not translating to retail activity.
